description:
MAINTAINER REPORT, 2026-08-13: 'the 1073k cap for ph, ps flash is too low for a htgr, which can produce very high temperature steam.'

Correct, and the situation is better than the cap implies -- most of the work is already done.

WHAT THE CAP ACTUALLY IS. 1073.15 K (800 degC) is NOT the limit of IAPWS-IF97. It is the limit of Regions 1-4.
IF97 Region 5 covers 1073.15 K to 2273.15 K at 0 < p <= 50 MPa. What Region 5 does NOT have is BACKWARD equations:
the standard provides no closed-form (p,h) -> T or (p,s) -> T there. That is the entire reason for the cap.

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR -- IT PANICS, it does not error:
  crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/interfaces/functional_programming/ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs:51
      FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => panic!("temperature: {}", REGION_5_PH_UNSUPPORTED)
  same file :141 for specific volume; ps_flash_eqm/mod.rs has the same pattern.
A panic, not a Result -- so a caller cannot recover, and this is the mechanism by which a large htgr_sim_v1
excursion dies once the steel property range was widened (see op-szmi.17, which records the failure relocating to
the steam side).

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, and makes this tractable:
  crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/region_5_steam_at_800_plus_degc/ implements the FORWARD equations --
  v_tp_5, u_tp_5, s_tp_5, cp_tp_5, cv_tp_5, w_tp_5, kappa_tp_5, alpha_v_tp_5, plus tau_5/pi_5.
  The (p,T) flash already routes Region 5 correctly and is verified at the envelope corners
  (see pt_flash_eqm/envelope_corner_tests.rs: 1073.15 K / 50 MPa -> Region5, h = 3.926050140e6, etc).

THE FIX. Invert the forward equation numerically. At fixed p, h_tp_5(T,p) is monotone increasing in T, so a
bracketed 1-D root find over [1073.15 K, 2273.15 K] is unconditionally convergent -- bisection or Brent, no Newton
needed and no risk of stepping outside the envelope. Same for (p,s) with s_tp_5. This is the standard treatment
where IF97 gives no backward equation, and it is what other IF97 implementations do.
  - State the tolerance and the iteration cap, and return an error rather than panicking if it is not met.
  - Above 2273.15 K or 50 MPa the state is genuinely outside IF97; REFUSE it explicitly, do not extrapolate.
  - Cost: an iterative flash is much dearer than a backward equation, and the SG calls the flash per node per
    substep. Region 5 should be the exceptional branch, not the common path -- measure it and say so.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THIS PROJECT. 1073.15 K = 800 degC. HTR-10 phase 1 (700 degC helium) stays clear. HTR-10 PHASE 2
IS 900 degC, and a once-through SG with a small pinch can put steam near the cap; the GTHTR300 line
(op-id3l.12) is hotter still. Beyond design operation, any excursion crosses it -- and today that is a hard panic
that kills the physics thread rather than a diagnosable error.

RELATED, and should be coordinated rather than duplicated:
  op-t647 (P0) -- bounds-checked IF97 facade returning Result. THIS BEAD IS THE OTHER HALF: op-t647 makes the
    boundary return an error instead of panicking; this one MOVES the boundary from 1073.15 K to 2273.15 K. Both
    are wanted, and the error-vocabulary decision in op-ffg6.1 should cover them together.
  op-szmi.17 -- records that widening the steel range relocates the failure to the steam side. This is that side.

notes.content:
CORRECTION to the description, 2026-08-13: I wrote that ps_flash_eqm 'has the same pattern' as ph_flash_eqm. It does not, and the difference matters for how each is fixed. Verified:

  ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs -- 2 sites, explicit panic! with a named constant:
      :51   FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => panic!("temperature: {}", REGION_5_PH_UNSUPPORTED)
      :141  same for specific volume
    So (p,h) is a DELIBERATE, documented refusal.

  ps_flash_eqm/mod.rs -- 2 sites, bare todo!():
      :64   FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => todo!("region 5 ps flash not implemented")
      :154  FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => todo!("ps flash not implemented for region 5")
    So (p,s) is UNIMPLEMENTED rather than refused, and the file's own docs acknowledge it at :463
    ('todo! panics in t_ps_eqm/v_ps_eqm').
    That file also carries two further unconditional panics, :828 'p,s point is outside pressure range' and
    :833 'p,s point below 273.15K' -- both are validity refusals that should return an error, and belong with
    op-t647 rather than here.

Both still panic and both still cap the useful envelope at 1073.15 K, so the bead's substance stands. The fix is
also the same numerically -- a bracketed 1-D root find on the monotone forward equation, h_tp_5 for (p,h) and
s_tp_5 for (p,s), over [1073.15 K, 2273.15 K]. Note s_tp_5 is already present and already routed on the (p,s) side
(ps_flash_eqm:264+ dispatches Region 5 for u, h, cp, cv, w), so the forward half is in place there too.

SUGGESTED ORDER: convert the two todo!()s to the same explicit, named refusal the (p,h) side uses FIRST -- a small,
safe change that makes the boundary honest and removes two todo!() panics -- then implement the inversion for both
together.

title: IF97 (p,h) and (p,s) flash panic above 1073.15 K -- too low for an HTGR, and Region 5 forward eqns already exist

description:
Condenser (components/condenser.rs:17) has only pressure: Pressure and target_outlet_quality: f64 (a bare f64 -- every other fraction in the layer is a uom Ratio; worth fixing while here). Zero geometry.

Part of op-dt3.17. The digital-twin widget layer must derive a component's on-screen size from its REAL dimensions; the engine crate forbids new physics, so the dimension must exist here in tampines.

DO NOT use HemSteamCv::get_volume() as a size -- it is the thermodynamic control volume, caller-supplied and unvalidated, conventionally a 1 m3 dummy (get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3). It describes the fluid parcel, not the machine.

Prefer explicit named dimensions where shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where only a rough size correlation is wanted. Document units and valid ranges in the doc comment per the workspace human-interface rule, and keep uom types.
title: tampines Condenser: add shell/envelope dimensions

description:
CoolingTower (components/cooling_tower.rs:19) has air_inlet: HumidAirState, water_inlet_temperature, water_flow_rate: VolumeRate, target_approach. Zero geometry.

Two traps: water_flow_rate is m3/s, a RATE not a volume; and air_inlet.volume is SpecificVolume (m3/kg), also not a size. Neither may be used for visual scale.

Cooling towers are the largest objects on a real plant and there is currently nothing to size them with.

Part of op-dt3.17. The digital-twin widget layer must derive a component's on-screen size from its REAL dimensions; the engine crate forbids new physics, so the dimension must exist here in tampines.

DO NOT use HemSteamCv::get_volume() as a size -- it is the thermodynamic control volume, caller-supplied and unvalidated, conventionally a 1 m3 dummy (get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3). It describes the fluid parcel, not the machine.

Prefer explicit named dimensions where shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where only a rough size correlation is wanted. Document units and valid ranges in the doc comment per the workspace human-interface rule, and keep uom types.
title: tampines CoolingTower: add shell height/diameter dimensions

description: Per the 2026-08-11 CLAUDE.md literature rule (commit 0857f5ea): the njoy-outram-park-fork thermal-scattering work cites ENDF-102 semantics in doc comments (src/endf/interp.rs law table 0.5.2; src/thermr/mf7.rs MF7 MT2/MT4 LT/LI record layouts, 7.2/7.4), but ENDF-102 is not in crates/kovan-literature/CATALOGUE.md (checked 2026-08-11, no match for 'ENDF-102' or 'formats manual'). The implementation itself was cross-checked against upstream NJOY2016 Fortran (endf.f90 terp1, thermr.f90 rdelas/calcem - source code, in-repo at the porting reference, not a publication) and against the raw ENDF/B-VIII.0 graphite tapes (data, exempt from the rule), so no uncited formula was taken from a publication from model memory; but the ENDF-102 section references in doc comments currently point at nothing in the archive. TODO: obtain the ENDF-102 manual PDF (CSEWG/BNL publication, e.g. the ENDF-6 Formats Manual, latest revision), decide access tier from its own copyright page (US national-lab report - likely open, but VERIFY, unsure means proprietary), kovan lit import, add to CATALOGUE.md, and confirm the section numbers cited in njoy doc comments against the actual document.
title: kovan-literature: catalogue ENDF-102 (ENDF-6 Formats Manual) - cited by njoy thermal-scattering code, not in archive
